skill.name: mcp-builder
skill.description: Deprecated guide for building Model Context Protocol servers with the mcp-use framework. Covers tools, resources, prompts, response helpers, resource templates, and React widget patterns.
skill.summary: Deprecated mcp-use guide for MCP tools, resources, prompts, and widgets.
skill.author: shubhamsaboo

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown examples, TypeScript template literals, localhost URLs, and documented environment variables. One external install command is confirmed because the deprecated skill directs users to install a replacement skill with npx. Semantic review also found a model-sampling prompt pattern that should treat tool input as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: The skill description redirects users to install another skill with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the install command or replace it with a reviewed marketplace migration note.

remediation.issue: A sampling example inserts tool input directly into the model prompt.
remediation.suggestion: Delimit user data and instruct the model to treat it only as data before calling ctx.sample.

remediation.issue: The weather API example places an API key in a URL query string.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer provider-supported authorization headers and warn authors not to log secret-bearing URLs.

semantic_findings.title: Deprecated Skill Redirects to External Install
semantic_findings.description: The skill description says it is deprecated and tells users to install mcp-app-builder with an npx command. This can redirect users or agents from the reviewed package to external code with separate trust assumptions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The redirect and install command are explicit in the skill description. No automatic execution was found, so the risk depends on user or agent action.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Tool Input Used In Sampling Prompt
semantic_findings.description: The tool context example passes user-provided data directly into ctx.sample without delimiters or data-only instructions. Generated servers that follow this pattern could let tool input steer the sampled model response.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example directly interpolates the data parameter into a model prompt. It is an instructional example, so impact depends on generated downstream code.

content.value_statement: Building MCP servers requires consistent patterns for tools, resources, prompts, and widgets. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for mcp-use projects.
actual_capabilities: Guides server tool, resource, and prompt definitions for mcp-use.
Explains resource templates for parameterized MCP data access.
Shows response helper choices for text, objects, markdown, HTML, media, and widgets.
Provides React widget patterns for interactive MCP interfaces.
Documents environment variable examples and server startup patterns.
Includes evaluation scenarios for implementation, architecture, widgets, and skill behavior.
limitations: The source skill is deprecated in favor of mcp-app-builder.
It provides guidance and examples, not a complete generated project.
External API examples require user-provided keys and provider review.
Production code still needs security review, validation, and tests.

use_cases.title: Create a Simple MCP Tool
use_cases.description: Build a typed tool with schema descriptions, response helpers, and clear error handling.

use_cases.title: Design MCP Resources
use_cases.description: Choose between tools, static resources, and parameterized resource templates for data access.

use_cases.title: Add Interactive Widgets
use_cases.description: Plan React widget files, widget metadata, and tool responses for visual MCP workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Build My First Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a basic MCP tool for my task. Include the schema fields, response type, and error behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Server Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan an MCP server for my app. Separate tools, resources, prompts, widgets, and required environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Widget Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an MCP widget workflow. Define the tool input, widget props, visible output, and user actions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my MCP server design. Check schemas, resource templates, widget state, external APIs, and security controls.

output_examples.input: Create a weather MCP tool with a visual result.
output: A typed tool plan with city input and missing-key error behavior.
A widget response plan with weather props and concise model-visible text.
A note to keep the API key in an environment variable.

output_examples.input: Design resources for user profiles and posts.
output: A resource template plan for user profile lookups.
A nested resource template plan for user post lookups.
Guidance on when a read-only resource is better than a tool.

output_examples.input: Review my MCP server before release.
output: A checklist covering schema descriptions, error responses, widget state, and environment variables.
Security notes for external APIs, destructive tools, and untrusted input.

best_practices: Use descriptive schemas and validation for every tool, prompt, and resource parameter.
Keep secrets in environment variables and document required values with safe examples.
Return clear model-visible output while keeping widget props focused on UI state.
anti_patterns: Do not use a tool when a read-only resource is enough.
Do not pass untrusted input into model sampling without boundaries and instructions.
Do not ship destructive tools without clear annotations and confirmation behavior.

faq.question: Is this skill current?
faq.answer: The source marks this skill as deprecated and points users toward mcp-app-builder.

faq.question: What framework does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers MCP server patterns using the mcp-use framework.

faq.question: Can it create widgets?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for React TSX widget files, widget metadata, and tool responses.

faq.question: Does it include complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that still need implementation work.

faq.question: How should API keys be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables, document required names, and avoid exposing secrets in logs or URLs.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Developers who maintain older mcp-use MCP server examples may find it useful.
